title: Extension of torsion frames over a normal base
statement:
Let $S$ be a normal locally Noetherian scheme, meaning that $S$ has an affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [pqf-def-locnoeth] and each local ring is an integrally closed domain, and let $j:V\hookrightarrow S$ be a dense open immersion. Let $N\to S$ be a separated smooth commutative group algebraic space of finite presentation, with geometrically connected fibres that are extensions of abelian varieties by tori, and assume $N_V$ is an abelian scheme. Here separated means that the diagonal $N\to N\times_S N$ is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A torus becomes a product of multiplicative groups over a separable closure; an abelian variety is a smooth proper geometrically connected group variety. Let $n\geq1$ be invertible on $S$, let $r\geq0$, and write $N[n]=\ker([n]:N\to N)$ as an etale sheaf: on an etale $T\to S$ its sections are those $x\in N(T)$ with $nx=0$. The restriction map
$$N[n]\longrightarrow j_*j^{-1}N[n]$$
is injective. For any isomorphism $\alpha:N_V[n]\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r}_V$ there is a unique monomorphism of etale sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-modules
$$\bar\alpha:N[n]\hookrightarrow\underline{(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r}_S$$
restricting to $\alpha$. It is natural under base isomorphisms and isomorphisms of $N$ carrying the specified open frame to the specified open frame; the target carries the identity action on its constant labels. Algebraic spaces, etale sites, inverse and direct image, and constant sheaves are [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; module sheaves are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-normal-etale-components-clopen] to the identity of $S$. Its hypotheses hold by the explicitly stated locally Noetherian and normal assumptions. Thus the irreducible components $S_a$ of $S$ are open and closed. Every local ring of $S$ is a domain, hence reduced; reducedness is detected on stalks, so $S$ and each open $S_a$ are reduced. Each nonempty $S_a$ is therefore integral, with the same integrally closed local rings as $S$. Density of $V$ implies that $V_a=V\cap S_a$ is nonempty for each $a$. These components are pairwise disjoint: if $S_a$ meets $S_b$, their intersection is a nonempty subset both open and closed in the irreducible space $S_a$, so it equals $S_a$. Thus $S_a\subseteq S_b$, and maximality makes the components equal. Thus they form a disjoint open cover of $S$. If $S$ is empty, its etale site has only the empty scheme as an object, all module sheaves have the unique zero section, and both assertions and uniqueness hold.

source.place: Tag 0357, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles; normality and reducedness from local rings (Tag 033K).

proof.text: For every etale test scheme $q:T\to S$, $T$ is normal and in particular reduced. Indeed choose affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq T$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the localizations $A_{\mathfrak p}$ are the integrally closed local domains of $S$, so $A$ is a normal ring (normality of a ring means normality of all these localizations). The restricted affine morphism is etale, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal] says $B$ is normal. The same stalk-localization identification gives normal local domains at every point of $T$. Domains have no nonzero nilpotents, hence the structure sheaf of $T$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 033C, lemma-normal-goes-up, specialized to etale maps; Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves.

proof.text: Put $T_V=T\times_S V$. It is dense in every etale $T\to S$: any nonempty open $W\subseteq T$ has nonempty open image $q(W)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], so this image meets $V$, and $W$ meets $T_V$. If $x,y\in N[n](T)$ have equal restrictions to $T_V$, their equalizer is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $N/S$ along $(x,y):T\to N\times_S N$. By the meaning of a representable closed diagonal this is a closed subscheme $E\hookrightarrow T$. The closed subset $|E|$ contains the dense open $T_V$, hence equals $|T|$. On each affine open $A=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $T$, write $E\times_T A=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its underlying closed set is all of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, so every prime ideal contains $I$. Thus every element of $I$ is nilpotent; $R$ is reduced by step 2, hence $I=0$. These affine identifications show $E=T$, so $x=y$. The open immersion $j$ is etale, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies $j^{-1}N[n]$ with the restriction $N[n]|_V$ and, by its part 2, $\eta_T:N[n](T)\to(j_*j^{-1}N[n])(T)=N[n](T_V)$ (section formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]) with restriction along $T_V\to T$. Hence this proves injectivity of the unit $\eta:N[n]\to j_*j^{-1}N[n]$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.2(i), printed p.140; expanded closed-diagonal argument; Stacks Tag 03WT, lemma-etale-open.

proof.text: Let $M=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$, and let $c:\underline M_S\to j_*\underline M_V$ be $j_*(\gamma_j)\circ\eta_{\underline M_S}$, where $\gamma_j:j^{-1}\underline M_S\cong\underline M_V$ is the comparison of [def-weil-pbc-etale-set-constant-pullback-comparison] (natural in the coefficient, hence $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-linear). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] part 2, $c_T:\underline M_S(T)\to\underline M_V(T_V)$ is restriction along $T_V\to T$ followed by $\gamma_j$, and the same lemma applied to the open immersion $S_a\to S$ identifies the restriction of $\underline M_S$, $j_*\underline M_V$ and $c$ to $S_a$ with the corresponding objects for $V_a\subseteq S_a$. On each open integral normal component $S_a$ of step 1, apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-constant-generic-open-unit] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, module $M$, and nonempty open $V_a$. It gives invertibility of $c|_{S_a}$; the section formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] identifies this restriction with the stated componentwise unit. For each etale $T\to S$, the opens $T_a=T\times_S S_a$ form a disjoint cover of $T$. On each $T_a$ the componentwise inverse uniquely lifts a section on $T_a\times_S V$ to a section of $\underline M_S(T_a)$. These lifts glue uniquely on $T$, commute with restrictions by their uniqueness, and are inverse to $c_T$. This proves invertibility as a morphism of module sheaves, also for infinitely many components.

source.place: Tag 09Z5, lemma-push-constant-sheaf-from-open (2); Deligne Lemma 3.5.2(ii), printed p.140.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] part 1, $j^{-1}N[n]\cong N[n]|_V$, and the equality of the kernel-section formulas gives $N[n]|_V=N_V[n]$. Define $\bar\alpha=c^{-1}\circ j_*(\alpha)\circ\eta$. Direct image acts on sections by the given map $\alpha$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], so $j_*(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism with inverse $j_*(\alpha^{-1})$. Hence step 3 and the invertibility of $c$ imply that $\bar\alpha$ is injective on sections and is a monomorphism. All three factors are $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-linear. On an etale test scheme over $V$, restriction $T\times_S V=T$ makes $\eta$ and $c$ identities, so the displayed composite restricts to $\alpha$.

For any other module-sheaf morphism $\beta:N[n]\to\underline M_S$ restricting to $\alpha$, any etale $T\to S$, and any section $x$, restricting $\beta_T(x)$ to $T_V$ gives $\alpha_{T_V}(x|_{T_V})$. Since $c_T$ is bijective by step 4, this forces $\beta_T(x)=c_T^{-1}(\alpha_{T_V}(x|_{T_V}))=\bar\alpha_T(x)$. Thus uniqueness holds among all module-sheaf morphisms, not just monomorphisms. If $h:S\xrightarrow{\sim}S\prime$ carries $V$ to $V\prime$ and $u:N\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*N\prime$ carries the open frames to one another, both $\bar\alpha$ and $h^*(\bar\alpha\prime)\circ u[n]$ restrict to $\alpha$. Uniqueness makes them equal. This is precisely the asserted naturality, with identity on the labels $M$.
